content: Before using this medication, visually inspect the product for any particles or discoloration. If either is present, do not use the liquid. If you are using a frozen pre-mixed solution, thaw the bag at room temperature or in the refrigerator. If thawed in the refrigerator, allow the bag to sit at room temperature for at least one hour before use. Do not thaw the solution using a water bath or microwave. After thawing, shake the bag well and squeeze it to check for leaks. Discard the solution if the bag leaks. For optimal effectiveness, administer this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals. Continue using the medication for the full duration prescribed, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Common side effects may include swelling, redness, or pain at the injection site. This medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Rarely, this medication may cause a severe intestinal condition due to a bacteria called Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile), which can occur during treatment or weeks to months after treatment has stopped. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may lead to oral thrush or a new yeast infection. If ceftriaxone is mixed with a numbing agent (e.g., lidocaine) before injection into a muscle, it may rarely cause a serious blood condition called methemoglobinemia. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. Before using ceftriaxone, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other antibiotics (e.g., penicillins, cephalosporins), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Do not administer products containing calcium (e.g., IV solutions like Ringer’s solution, Hartmann’s solution, or parenteral nutrition) to newborns under one month old who are receiving this medication. Ceftriaxone may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines (e.g., typhoid vaccine). This medication passes into breast milk in small amounts but is unlikely to harm a nursing infant. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication may interfere with certain lab tests (e.g., urine glucose tests), potentially causing false results. If someone overdoses and experiences severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call emergency services (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center immediately. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. While using this medication, lab tests (e.g., complete blood count, kidney function tests) should be performed as directed by your healthcare provider. If you miss a dose, consult your doctor or pharmacist promptly for a new dosing schedule. For storage, refer to the product instructions or consult your pharmacist. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
